q: Which of the following finishes or fixtures would be the least expected choice in a high-end condominium unit?
o: Engineered wood flooring in the bedrooms
n: Luxury units are specified with split-type or centralized air conditioning for quieter operation and a cleaner facade; a window-type unit is a budget solution tied to entry-level projects, not high-end ones — per the source document.

q: In a condominium unit that has only a single window, which space should ideally be placed beside that window?
n: When a compact unit has only one source of natural light and ventilation, that opening is prioritized for the bedroom, since occupants spend extended hours there and need daylight and air circulation most directly — per the source document's unit-planning guidance.

q: All of the following influence how elevators are sized and specified for a high-rise residential project, EXCEPT:
o: The projected population of the building
The target travel speed of the car
The total number of floors served
The overall height of the building
n: Elevator sizing and specification are driven by traffic-design inputs — building height, population, floors served, and target car speed. "PSOmax" is not a recognized elevator traffic-design parameter, so it is the one item that does not factor in — per the source document.

q: Which use is most compatible for mixing with high-rise residential floors within a single building?
n: Retail and commercial space is the classic podium use paired with residential towers — it activates the ground levels and serves residents without the noise, traffic, or operating-hour conflicts of office, industrial, institutional, or school uses — per standard mixed-use planning practice in the source document.

q: The Fire Code requires all of the following to be located in the fire command center, EXCEPT:
o: Controls to simultaneously unlock stairway doors
Fire detection and alarm annunciator panel
All of the items above belong in the fire command center
Sprinkler valve and water-flow display panels
n: The fire command center consolidates the alarm annunciator, sprinkler/water-flow monitoring, voice communication system, and stairway door-release controls in one place for staff to monitor and operate during an emergency — none of the listed items is excluded — per RA 9514, Fire Code of the Philippines.

q: Which of the following amenities would you be least likely to find in a low-end or economically priced condominium development?
n: Entry-level projects typically economize on individual unit fit-out and rely on window-type units instead; split-type air conditioning is the step up associated with mid- to high-end projects, even though shared amenities like a pool or lobby are still commonly provided — per the source document.

q: Stepping through the front door of a studio-type condominium unit, which area is typically the first one you encounter?
n: In the typical studio layout, the kitchen sits nearest the entry so wet, service-heavy activities stay close to the plumbing stack and away from the sleeping and living zones at the far end of the unit — per the source document's studio-layout guidance.

q: Under RA 9514, which of the following is NOT a feature required in every building that qualifies as high-rise?
o: All of the above are required in every high-rise building
n: Sprinklers, smoke control in protected spaces, and fire-rated stair enclosures are baseline life-safety requirements applied across high-rise buildings, but a dedicated fire command center is only mandated once a building crosses additional height/occupancy thresholds — per RA 9514, Fire Code of the Philippines.

q: What kitchen configuration is most commonly used in a studio condominium unit?
o: Any of these — it varies by owner
n: A studio unit's limited floor area normally reduces the kitchen to a single run of counter and cabinetry along one wall, the layout that uses the least floor space among standard kitchen configurations — per the source document.

q: Which statement correctly describes good practice in laying out a high-rise condominium floor plate?
o: Both the constant-width principle and the corner-placement principle apply
The unit width (short dimension) should stay constant across unit types
Both the constant-depth principle and the corner-placement principle apply
The unit depth (long dimension) should stay constant across unit types
Larger units (2BR, 3BR) should be positioned at the building corners
n: Standard condo-planning practice keeps unit depth uniform across the floor plate so the structural grid and envelope repeat efficiently, varying only the frontage width, with premium larger units placed at corners to capture two exposures — per the source document's floor-plate planning guidance.
